robot.name: AgiBot X2
robot.status_notes: Base X2 is purchasable on AgiBot's official international store for $24,240 (verified by Robozaps in July 2026); China Youth Edition lists at ¥98,000. X2 Ultra, X2 Pro and X2 Edu are quote-only or price-on-request. The base X2 does not support secondary development. No named customer deployment with operating metrics was found.
intended_use_cases: elderly care (initial deployment focus per TMTPost)

height.notes: Officially listed as 1310 mm about 1.31 m. X2 and X2 Ultra share same dimensions.

weight.notes: Base X2 weight used as primary value; Ultra is heavier.

payload.original_value: Max (in specific postures): 3kg; Across full range: ≤1kg (excluding end effector)
payload.notes: Payload excludes end effector and varies by posture.

runtime.notes: Runtime estimate from official product page; speed and tasks affect actual endurance.

battery.notes: Official product page lists approx. 500Wh. Robozaps reports the X2 Ultra SDK documentation lists ~421Wh, conflicting; delivery configuration should be confirmed.

degrees_of_freedom.notes: Base X2 has 25 total DoF; X2 Ultra has 30 total DoF; X2 Edu is claimed at 29 DoF by Center 3D Print. Third-party sources mention 27, 28, 31, 39 counts, but official product page and Robozaps use 25/30.

walking_speed.original_value: Up to 1.8 m/s; typical ≤0.8 m/s; Laboratory Environment: ≤2m/s
walking_speed.notes: Peak speed 1.8 m/s; typical walking speed is 0.8 m/s or less.

hands.description: End-effectors (Omnihand, OmniPicker) are only compatible with X2 Ultra; not included as standard and must be purchased separately. No standard hand DoF or tactile details found for base X2.

items: X2: Interactive RGB camera, head touch sensor, microphone array, interactive screen
X2 Ultra adds 3D LiDAR, RGB-D camera, front dual RGB, rear RGB, 4G/5G module, same head touch sensor
X2 Edu optional sensors include cameras, LiDAR, IMU depending on configuration (reseller)

compute.description: Base X2: dual RK3588; X2 Ultra: dual RK3588 plus NVIDIA Orin NX (157 TOPS). X2 Edu listed with RK3588 and expandable computational part.

actuators.description: Peak joint torque 120 N·m. No actuator type or vendor disclosed in reviewed sources.

availability.notes: Standard X2 is $24,240 on AgiBot's official international store, verified by Robozaps; shipping adds $500–$3,000, import duties on buyer, no returns after delivery. China Youth Edition ¥98,000 (~$14,500). X2 Ultra quote-only; Generation Robots lists it from €56,400. X2 Pro quote-only; X2 Edu price on request.

manipulation_dexterity.summary: Official specifications list X2 arm reach 558 mm, peak joint torque 120 N·m, payload up to 3 kg in specific postures, and 5-DoF arms on base / 7-DoF arms on Ultra. X2 Ultra is compatible with Omnihand and OmniPicker end-effectors, which are sold separately. Public video titles mention mastering human motions and unboxing, but no transcript was reviewed; no independent dexterity benchmark or success rate found.
caveats: Base X2 does not support secondary development.
End-effectors are extra-cost options and only compatible with Ultra.
No real-world manipulation success rates or load-bearing validation beyond specs.

autonomy_task_execution.summary: Official page claims X2 Ultra supports autonomous navigation, proactive obstacle avoidance, and algorithm-driven decision-making; base X2 does not support these functions. TMTPost reports X2 targets task execution and autonomous operation, but Robozaps and Joybuy caution that many demos are choreographed or remotely controlled, and buyers must distinguish autonomy from remote control.
caveats: No independent verification of autonomy.
Teleoperation status is not disclosed in public video titles.
Autonomous functions are claimed for Ultra only, not base X2.

mobility_whole_body_control.summary: Official specs list walking speed up to 1.8 m/s (typical ≤0.8 m/s, laboratory ≤2 m/s), humanoid gait, complex dance routines, and 25–30 DoF including waist. Public video titles mention generalist human motions, but no transcript reviewed; Robozaps notes the bicycle demo was largely center-of-gravity physics rather than active balance.
caveats: No fall rate, disturbance recovery, or independent mobility benchmark.
Viral demos may be choreographed or human-assisted.

perception_scene_understanding.summary: X2 Ultra is equipped with 3D LiDAR, RGB-D camera, interactive RGB camera, front dual RGB and rear RGB; base X2 has interactive RGB camera only. Company claims precise 3D spatial perception, environmental semantic perception, and obstacle detection. X2 Edu configuration may include cameras, LiDAR and IMU.
caveats: Detection range, response time, and limitations under varied lighting not disclosed.
No perception benchmark or independent evaluation.

human_interaction.summary: Official page highlights multimodal interaction with visual, voice, tactile, and facial expression capabilities; includes head touch sensor, microphone array, speaker, interactive screen. Press release mentions WITA Omni end-to-end multimodal interaction model. TMTPost notes aim for rich emotional expressiveness and adaptive interaction.
caveats: No conversational reliability or instruction-following metric found.
WITA Omni is a company announcement, not specific X2 performance data.

endurance_reliability.summary: Specs: ~500 Wh battery, about 2 hours at 0.5 m/s walking, charging ≤1.5 hours, swappable battery. No long-duration reliability data, independent endurance test, or failure rate found.
caveats: Runtime is an estimate and depends on speed, load, sensors, and communications.
No real-world endurance data or uptime logs published.

human_environment_fit.summary: Compact 1.31 m / 35–39 kg form with operating temperature -10°C to 40°C. Joybuy warns professional users must plan safety perimeter, risk assessment, operator training and compliance. No full-robot safety certification found.
caveats: No safety certification or compliance documents verified.
User business must assess risks per local regulations.

deployment_commercial_proof.summary: X2 has a real international order route: base X2 listed at $24,240 on AgiBot's official international store, verified by Robozaps; distribution via RobotShop, Center3D and Generation Robots; AgiBot recruiting channel partners. TMTPost reports B2B2C sales strategy and target of several thousand units by end 2026. No specific customer deployments or operating hours published.
caveats: No named customer deployment with output metrics found.
Base X2 does not support secondary development, limiting enterprise integration.
Price verified by media, not by an independent audit.

accessibility_value.summary: Standard X2 is buyable at $24,240 plus $500–$3,000 shipping and duties, no returns after delivery; China Youth Edition ¥98,000. X2 Ultra quote-only (€56,400 via Generation Robots), X2 Pro quote-only, X2 Edu price on request. Robozaps verified the official store listing in July 2026.
caveats: No returns after delivery; buyer pays duties and taxes.
Base X2 lacks secondary development; research buyers need Ultra/Pro/Edu.
X2 Ultra $999,999 placeholder on store is not a real price.

evidence_items.title: Robozaps verified X2 price on official international store
evidence_items.claim: Robozaps verified the base X2 price of $24,240 on AgiBot's official international store, unchanged since at least April; shipping adds $500–$3,000 with duties on buyer.
evidence_items.notes: Third-party media verified the live listing.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Strongest evidence of real purchase availability.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: The AgiBot Lingxi X2 costs **$24,240 on AgiBot's official international store**, a price we verified directly on the live listing in July 2026, unchanged since at least April.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Robozaps is a reputable tech blog; verification not independently audited but direct.

evidence_items.title: Robozaps: base X2 lacks secondary development support
evidence_items.claim: Development access officially belongs to Ultra/Pro/Edu trims; base X2 at $24,240 does not support secondary development.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Caps research value of base model.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Development access officially belongs to the Ultra (and the Pro and Edu trims with their open interfaces), so buyers who want to write code against the robot should be quoting those, not the $24,240 base model.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Consistent with official product page statement that base X2 'Not supported' for secondary development.

evidence_items.title: Robozaps: viral demos often human-controlled
evidence_items.claim: Viral X2 demos including bicycle and hoverboard are real hardware but often choreographed; bicycle balance was largely center-of-gravity physics and several showcases were human-controlled.
evidence_items.notes: Caution against treating demos as autonomous.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Limits autonomy and mobility credit from demos.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: The honest caveat is about autonomy: in the bicycle demo, as reporting on the program later noted, the robot was mounted on the seat, keeping the bike upright largely through center-of-gravity physics rather than active balance algorithms, and several X2 event showcases have been described as human-controlled rather than autonomous.
evidence_items.source_location: Robozaps review, viral demos honestly assessed section
evidence_items.verification_notes: Media analysis based on reporting; no transcript of original demos.

evidence_items.arena_relevance: Indicates commercial ambition but not proof.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: "By the end of 2026, we hope to reach a scale of several thousand units," Wei said, with large-scale shipments expected to begin in the second half of this year.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Direct quote from Wei Qiang; target not audited.

evidence_items.notes: Company statement of intended use; no actual deployment yet.

evidence_items.title: Joybuy: autonomony cannot be assumed from demos
evidence_items.claim: Seeing a robot walk, wave or pick up an object is not enough to prove it can operate without human intervention; buyers must verify autonomy features separately.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Seeing a robot walk, wave or pick up an object is not enough to prove that it can operate without human intervention.

evidence_items.title: RobotShop Community: X2 series purpose
evidence_items.claim: X2 series includes two compact humanoid robots for interaction, service, and educational use; X2 optimized for interaction/performance, X2 Ultra for perception/autonomy/development.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: The **X2 Ultra** focuses on **perception**, **autonomous** **operation**, and **development**, while the **X2** is optimized for **interaction**, **performance**, and **accessible** **deployment**.

researcher_notes.short_verdict_for_arena: AgiBot X2 is a compact, purchasable service humanoid with a verified international price and clear variant structure. Strongest evidence is the official store listing and distribution network; weakest is autonomy and real-world deployment performance. Base X2 lacks secondary development; autonomous functions are claimed only for Ultra and remain unverified.
strongest_positive_evidence: Robozaps verified base X2 at $24,240 on official international store, with shipping and duty details.
Official product page provides detailed specs (DoF, sensors, compute, speed, payload, battery).
Distribution through RobotShop, Center3D and Generation Robots confirms commercial availability.
Compact 1.31 m, 35 kg form with multimodal interaction suite.
weakest_or_missing_evidence: No independent autonomy test, intervention log, or autonomous demo transcript.
No named customer deployment or operating metrics.
No independent reliability or endurance data.
Base X2 does not support secondary development.
Video titles only; no transcript reviewed.
conflicting_claims: DoF counts: official 25/30, TMTPost up to 31, Robozaps mentions 27/28/29/31/39, Center3D says X2 Edu 29.
Battery capacity: official ~500 Wh vs Robozaps note of Ultra SDK documentation ~421 Wh.
Price: $24,240 base, ¥98,000 China Youth, Ultra quote-only with a $999,999 placeholder on store (not real).
do_not_overclaim: Do not treat viral bicycle/dance demos as autonomous; Robozaps says often human-controlled.
Do not credit base X2 with autonomous navigation or obstacle avoidance; official page says not supported.
Do not use TMTPost 31 DoF as spec; official values are 25/30.
Do not treat $999,999 Ultra placeholder as a real price.
Do not claim customer deployments or elderly care rollout; only intended focus per TMTPost.

currentness.currentness_notes: AgiBot X2 is current compact interaction humanoid as of 2026-10-29. X2 Edu announced July 2026, not superseding base X2. No newer X-series replacement found in reviewed sources.

excluded_claims.reason: TMTPost says up to 31 DoF, but official product page and Robozaps state 25 base / 30 Ultra. Conflicting counts excluded from primary spec.
Robozaps reports SDK documentation says ~421 Wh, but official product page says approx. 500 Wh. Official value used in specs; conflict noted.
Robozaps identifies $999,999 as a quote-required placeholder, not a real price.
Robozaps cautions bicycle demo was center-of-gravity physics and event showcases were human-controlled; autonomy not verified.
Official product page lists Secondary Development 'Not supported' for base X2; Robozaps reiterates.
TMTPost quotes Wei Qiang saying initial deployment will focus on elderly living communities, but no named facility or actual deployment evidence found.

arena_prompt_summary.one_paragraph_summary: AgiBot X2 is a compact 1.31 m, 35 kg biped humanoid service robot from AgiBot (China). Official specs list 25 DoF base / 30 DoF Ultra, walking up to 1.8 m/s, 3 kg max payload, ~500 Wh battery, and multimodal interaction. The most important evidence is commercial availability: Robozaps verified the base X2 at $24,240 on AgiBot's official international store, with distribution via RobotShop, Center3D and Generation Robots. However, autonomy is unproven: base X2 officially lacks autonomous navigation, Ultra claims are company-only, and media caution that viral demos are often choreographed or human-controlled. No named customer deployment, operating hours, or independent performance benchmark was found. Secondary development is restricted to Ultra/Pro/Edu variants.
strongest_evidence: Verified purchase price and official store listing (agibot-x2_evidence_009).
Official product page with detailed specs (agibot-x2_evidence_001, _005).
Compact form factor with interaction sensors (agibot-x2_evidence_002).
weakest_evidence: No independent autonomy, navigation, or manipulation benchmark.
No transcript for any demo video.
